title: Arjun Rampal Is Playing a Fallen Billionaire. The Producer Just Admitted Who He's 'Loosely Based' On.
excerpt: Hansal Mehta's next is 'Billionaire', and the industry's worst-kept secret is finally semi-official: that swagger, that empire, that spectacular fall belong to a tycoon we all know the name of.
body:
Some casting just clicks before a single frame is shot. Put **Arjun Rampal** — all cheekbones, controlled menace, and that low, unbothered baritone — in a bespoke suit, hand him an empire and a private jet, and let the rot set in slowly. You already know how that movie feels. You've been watching it play out in the business pages for a decade.

Now it's a series. **Billionaire**, the Amazon MX Player original directed by **Hansal Mehta** and **Robbie Grewal**, has been the subject of feverish industry chatter since it was announced earlier this year: is Rampal playing a character modelled on **Vijay Mallya**, the flamboyant liquor baron turned fugitive whose Kingfisher empire collapsed into one of India's most theatrical financial scandals? For months the makers stayed coy. This week, producer **Prabhleen Sandhu** finally stopped pretending.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=zmRGno12Z7E</youtube>


![Vijay Mallya — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/5/54/Vijaymallya.jpg)



> **""We are currently working on a web series called *Billionaire*."**




> "It is loosely based on him. But it's not exactly about him." — Prabhleen Sandhu, on whether Arjun Rampal's character is inspired by Vijay Mallya

That's about as close to a confession as the OTT world ever gives you. Speaking to Bollywood Hungama while riding the acclaim of her recent *Made In India: A Titan Story*, Sandhu confirmed the project is rolling and named the dream-team behind it. "We are currently working on a web series called *Billionaire*. It was officially announced earlier this year. Hansal Mehta ji and Robbie Grewal are directing it," she said, before adding that her banner, Almighty Motion Picture, is also attached to an untitled Prime Video show.

The Mallya question, of course, was the one everyone actually wanted answered. And the "loosely based" phrasing is doing a lot of careful legal work. Earlier industry whispers had floated that the tycoon could be a composite — a little Mallya, a little **Lalit Modi**, a dash of every swaggering Indian magnate who flew too close to the sun. Sandhu's wording keeps that door cracked open: recognisable enough to sell, fictional enough to be safe.


![Prabhleen Sandhu — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/e7/Prabhleen_Sandhu_%28cropped%29.jpg)


What isn't ambiguous is the pedigree. Hansal Mehta is the man who turned real-life financial crime into prestige television with the *Scam* franchise — *Scam 1992* remains, for many, the gold standard of the Indian web series. He doesn't do cartoon villains. He does men who believe their own myth right up until the moment it eats them. Pair that sensibility with Grewal's craft and a logline about "a powerful business magnate who reshapes the rules to build an empire driven by ambition and influence," and you can practically smell the boardroom cigars and the impending collapse.

Rampal, for his part, arrives at exactly the right moment. He's on a genuine high after **Dhurandhar**, the role that reminded everyone the man can do more than glower handsomely — he can hold a screen with real gravity. "He's on a high after *Dhurandhar*," Sandhu said warmly. "We are happy to be working with him." Amazon's content head **Amogh Dusad** put it more grandly at the announcement, crediting Rampal with bringing "gravitas and intensity to this compelling character." Translation: they want you to watch a beautiful man build something enormous and then watch it burn.

It's a smart bet on a very specific appetite. The diaspora has an almost insatiable hunger for the rise-and-fall tycoon drama — the Indian *Succession*, the desi *Wolf of Wall Street*. There's a particular satisfaction, watching from a flat in London or a suburb outside Toronto, in seeing the gilded excess and moral decay of the homeland's super-rich rendered in glossy, bingeable form. Mallya himself — the parties, the cricket team, the calendar girls, the spectacular flight from creditors — was always going to end up dramatised. The only surprise is that it took this long.

Written by **Anubhav Chopra** and **Shantanu Sagara**, *Billionaire* is set against the backdrop of a rapidly changing India, tracing how the same forces that build a man's empire begin to consume his personal and professional world. For NRI viewers, the platform is the good news: Amazon MX Player is a free, ad-supported service, and while it streams primarily within India, the show's profile and Mehta's pull make a wider international rollout or Prime Video crossover the kind of thing the diaspora should keep an eye on.

No release date yet, no first look, no teaser. Just a director who knows how empires fall, an actor finally being trusted with weight, and a producer who said the quiet part just loud enough. "Loosely based on him." Sure. We'll see how loose it really is.
